name: Create Order
overview: [excited] Okay..., so we're on the Order form now! Think of this as the plan that tells us what linen goes out..., what comes back..., and when. [friendly] Let's walk through it together — it's pretty straightforward once you see it![chuckles]

nodes.label: Order Reference ID
nodes.explanation: [casual] This is just a unique name for the order. You can type your own… or leave it blank and the system will generate one for you automatically.
nodes.tips: [thoughtful] Something like ORD-2026-001 works really well — keeps things nice and easy to find later.

commonQuestions.question: What happens if I leave this blank?
commonQuestions.answer: The system will auto-generate a reference ID when you save the order.

commonQuestions.question: Can I use any format?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes, you can use any format. But a consistent pattern like ORD-YYYY-NNN makes orders easier to find.

nodes.label: Customer
nodes.explanation: [friendly] Just start typing the customer's name and pick them from the list. Simple as that! If they're not showing up… they might be inactive.
nodes.tips: [thoughtful] Head over to the Customers page and make sure they're marked as active — that's usually the reason.

commonQuestions.question: Why can't I find my customer?
commonQuestions.answer: Only active customers appear in the search. Check the Customers page to make sure the customer is active and not deactivated.

commonQuestions.question: Can I create a new customer from here?
commonQuestions.answer: No, you need to create the customer first from the Customers page, then come back to create the order.

nodes.label: Order Date
nodes.explanation: [casual] This is just the date the order's being created. It defaults to today… so most of the time, you won't even need to touch it.
nodes.tips: [thoughtful] Only change it if you're backdating an older order that was missed.

commonQuestions.question: Can I set a past date?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes, you can set a past order date. The pickup and delivery dates will adjust to maintain the same number of days between them.

nodes.label: Order Type
nodes.explanation: [curious] Okay, THIS one is really important. It tells the whole system what kind of order this is. Leasing is your everyday order… Rental is for short-term use… and Washing is when a customer sends in their OWN linen to be cleaned.
nodes.tips: [thoughtful] Whatever you pick here will actually change which fields appear below — so make sure it's right before moving on.

commonQuestions.question: What is the difference between Leasing and Rental?
commonQuestions.answer: Leasing is for long-term linen contracts where items are delivered and picked up on a schedule. Rental is short-term, like an event or a one-time use.

commonQuestions.question: What does Washing mean?
commonQuestions.answer: A Washing order is when the customer sends their own linen to your facility for cleaning. You pick it up, wash it, and deliver it back.

nodes.label: Adjustment Order
nodes.explanation: [casual] For a brand new order… just leave this off. You'd only switch it on if you're going back to fix or update something in an existing order.
nodes.tips: When in doubt, leave it off — it's rarely needed for day-to-day orders. [chuckles]

commonQuestions.question: When should I use Adjustment Order?
commonQuestions.answer: Use it when you need to correct or modify an existing order, like adding items that were missed or adjusting quantities.

nodes.label: Delivery Type
nodes.explanation: [curious] So… are we dropping off linen, picking it up, or doing BOTH in the same trip? For most leasing customers, it's Both — fresh linen goes out while the used stuff comes back.
nodes.tips: [friendly] If you're not sure, Both is almost always the right call for leasing orders.

commonQuestions.question: What if I only need to pick up items?
commonQuestions.answer: Choose 'Pickup' and the system will only show pickup-related fields and items.

nodes.label: Pickup Date
nodes.explanation: [casual] This is the day your team heads out to collect the used linen. It defaults to tomorrow… just change it if your schedule's different.
nodes.tips: [thoughtful] Just double-check it's not landing on a weekend or holiday… unless your team's working that day.

commonQuestions.question: Can the pickup date be before the order date?
commonQuestions.answer: Technically yes, but it's unusual. The system allows it for edge cases like backdating.

nodes.label: Delivery Date
nodes.explanation: [casual] And this is when the fresh linen gets delivered to the customer. Also defaults to tomorrow — adjust it if needed.
nodes.tips: [thoughtful] Make sure the warehouse has enough time to get everything ready before this date rolls around.

commonQuestions.question: What if delivery is delayed?
commonQuestions.answer: You can edit the order later to change the delivery date. The system does not automatically reschedule.

nodes.name: Delivery Item

autoPopulatedTrigger.description: Products auto-populate based on the customer's reserved products after selection

fallbackManual.description: Click this if no products auto-populate for the selected customer

nodes.explanationForMultiple: [friendly] You can add as many items as the order needs — let me show you a second one real quick.
nodes.explanation: [excited] Now we're adding the actual linen items going out to the customer! Good news — these usually fill in automatically based on what's in their agreement.

children.label: Product
children.explanation: [casual] Pick the product being delivered. Only items from the customer's agreement will show up here.

children.label: Quantity
children.explanation: How many are going out this cycle? Just type the number.

children.label: Remarks
children.explanation: [casual] Got any special instructions for this item? Things like quality requirements or handling notes — pop them in here.

nodes.name: Pickup Item

copyFrom.checkboxLabel: Use same items and quantities as Delivery

nodes.explanationForMultiple: [friendly] Let me add a second pickup item to show you how it works.
nodes.explanation: [casual] Now for what's coming BACK. If it's the same items as the delivery… just tick that checkbox and it'll copy everything over automatically. Super handy!

children.label: Product
children.explanation: Which product are we collecting from the customer?

children.label: Quantity
children.explanation: [thoughtful] How many are we picking up? This can be different from the delivery if they're still holding onto some.

children.label: Remarks
children.explanation: [casual] Anything the team should know on the way back? Damaged items, special handling — just note it here.

nodes.name: Rental Item
nodes.explanation: [friendly] Here's where we add what's being rented out — the product, how many, and how long they're keeping it. Easy stuff!

children.label: Product
children.explanation: What product is going out on rental?

children.label: Quantity
children.explanation: How many units are they renting?

children.label: Rental Duration (days)
children.explanation: [casual] And how many days are they keeping it? Just type the number of days.

nodes.name: Washing Item
nodes.explanation: [casual] For a washing order, just add what the customer sent in to be cleaned — the product type and how many pieces. That's all there is to it.

children.label: Product
children.explanation: Which product did they send in for washing?

children.label: Quantity
children.explanation: And how many pieces came in? Just type the count.

wrapUp: [warm and satisfied] And that's a wrap! [chuckles] We covered the customer, order type, dates, and all the items. Nothing was actually saved during this walkthrough… so whenever you're ready, go ahead and create your first REAL order. You've got this!
description: Walkthrough for creating a new leasing, rental, or washing order
